description: Settings that follow the account across its devices. They travel on GET and PUT /api/v1/account/settings, never in sync_changes, so an older server image keeps working. A client that does not see the capability keeps every setting on the device.

query.afterRevision: integer >= 0, default 0; keys whose revision is greater. 0 leaves out cleared keys

response.items: [{key, value | null, revision, updatedAt}] ordered by revision
response.hasMore: continue with afterRevision = last item revision

request.changes: 1-100 of {key, value | null, baseRevision >= 0, ifAbsent?: boolean}; the whole batch is refused when one change is invalid (unknown key SETTINGS_KEY_UNKNOWN, oversized SETTINGS_VALUE_TOO_LARGE 413, wrong value VALIDATION_ERROR), or when a new key would exceed the account cap (SETTINGS_TOO_MANY_KEYS)

response.revision: the account head revision after the write
response.results: [{key, status: applied, revision} | {key, status: kept | conflict, current: {value, revision}}]

put.conflicts: server-wins per key: a baseRevision other than the stored revision (0 when the key is absent) changes nothing and returns the stored value. ifAbsent inserts only a key the account never held (a cleared key counts as held) and otherwise returns kept

revisions: every applied change takes the next number of the account head counter, so revisions are distinct and increase for the life of the account

keys.recordedBy: {version: 1, mode: primaryProfile | custom | personTakingIt, customName?: string 1-60 trimmed} strict
keys.today.noticesLater: [{medicationId: uuid, until: YYYY-MM-DD}] up to 500; the client prunes past days
keys.appearance.text: {fontSize: defaultSize | large | extraLarge, highContrast: bool, reduceMotion: bool} strict
keys.appearance.colors: {light, dark} strict; each a partial map of the 21 colour roles to an opaque ARGB integer 0xff000000-0xffffffff
keys.language: system or a BCP-47 shaped tag such as ro or pt-BR
